items.topic: Disposition of orphan deliverables (operational baseline defaults, integration smoke harness, PRD fill-out, runbook)
items.context: Round 1's retirement choice leaves four deliverables from the prior integration-milestone plan without an owner: (1) operational baseline defaults — max concurrent sessions, Xvfb display number range, session TTL, per-session resource ceilings; (2) Phase 1 integration smoke harness (e.g., `make phase1-ready`); (3) PRD.md fill-out for `scenarios/vrooli-emulator/`; (4) operator runbook at `scenarios/vrooli-emulator/docs/runbook.md`. PRD + runbook have a natural home in `chore/vrooli-emulator-documentation`. Operational baseline values are really config defaults that want to be both documented and validated. Integration smoke is arguably a special case of the acceptance suite. We need to decide a disposition for all four before closing this item.

options.label: Split across existing siblings: PRD + runbook + baseline-values-as-docs → `chore/vrooli-emulator-documentation`; integration smoke + distro matrix → `execute/emulator-acceptance-tests-phase-1`
options.rationale: Every orphan lands in a sibling whose scope already covers the same domain. No new backlog item needed. Documentation chore already scoped for operator-facing content; acceptance tests already scoped for end-to-end validation. Minimum churn.

options.label: Create a new sibling `execute/vrooli-emulator-operational-baseline` to own the baseline defaults + integration smoke; PRD + runbook still fold into `chore/vrooli-emulator-documentation`
options.rationale: Isolates operational readiness as its own accountable item rather than mixing it into acceptance tests. Cleaner ownership but adds a 14th item to the initiative and another workshop cycle.

options.label: Fold all four into `chore/vrooli-emulator-documentation` (including integration smoke as a documented verification procedure)
options.rationale: Single-target rehoming. Downside: integration smoke really is a scripted test, not docs — placing it in a chore item misrepresents its nature and may get deprioritized.

options.label: Drop orphan work entirely — let `execute/adopt-vrooli-emulator-in-deployment-flows` discover needs as it attempts adoption
options.rationale: Smallest-scope retirement. Risky: adopter item hits operational gaps during integration and has to scramble. Explicitly listed as a known-High-impact risk in §11.

options.label: Other — I'll specify disposition in freeform
options.rationale: Describe your disposition for each of the four orphans.

items.topic: New `depends_on` set for `execute/adopt-vrooli-emulator-in-deployment-flows` after removing this umbrella edge
items.context: The adopt item currently depends on this umbrella. With retirement, we need to replace that single edge with direct dependencies on the Phase 1 sibling items that actually gate adoption. The adopt item's job is to rewire scenario-to-desktop and deployment-manager to consume the new emulator service, so its prereqs should be: the emulator service works, its consumer-facing surfaces exist, and the old code path is gone.

options.label: Comprehensive: add `execute/emulator-acceptance-tests-phase-1`, `execute/vrooli-emulator-external-url-endpoint`, `execute/scenario-to-desktop-emulator-iframe-embed`, `chore/scenario-to-desktop-remove-livedesktop`, `chore/vrooli-emulator-documentation`
options.rationale: All five Phase 1 gates must be green before the adopter starts: tests prove the service works, external-url + iframe-embed give s2d its replacement UI, livedesktop removal clears the old stack, docs give operators what they need. Under-specifying this is harder to reverse than over-specifying since adopt is a one-shot gate.

options.label: Integration-focused: add only `execute/emulator-acceptance-tests-phase-1`, `execute/vrooli-emulator-external-url-endpoint`, `execute/scenario-to-desktop-emulator-iframe-embed`
options.rationale: The three that mechanically gate s2d integration. Leaves out livedesktop-removal (chore sibling can run in parallel with adopt) and docs (nice-to-have but not blocking). Risk: adopt finishes before old stack is cleaned up → dual-run window.

options.label: Minimal: add only `execute/emulator-acceptance-tests-phase-1` + `chore/scenario-to-desktop-remove-livedesktop`
options.rationale: Smallest gate — service proven working, old stack gone. Assumes adopt item can absorb integration work (external-url + iframe embed) as part of its own scope. Downside: double-owns integration surface with its sibling items.

options.rationale: Describe the exact set you want.

items.topic: Retire mechanism — archive this item (status change) vs delete outright
items.context: Two ways to remove this item from the active backlog. `swarm-manager backlog update --data '{"status":"archived"}'` preserves spec.json, plan.md, workshop rounds, and validation report — the item becomes a historical artifact that still grep-matches but shouldn't appear in active queues. `swarm-manager backlog delete` removes the directory entirely. Either way, active processing stops.

options.label: Archive (status=archived) — preserves plan + retirement rationale + round history as a historical record
options.rationale: Keeps an audit trail of WHY this was retired. If someone later asks 'what happened to the emulator umbrella?' the answer is in the files. Low cost, non-destructive, aligns with the project's no-git-mutations feedback posture (nothing is destroyed). Also preserves the `acceptance_allow` globs as reference if the umbrella is ever resurrected.

options.label: Delete outright via `swarm-manager backlog delete`
options.rationale: Cleanest removal — no lingering directory, no grep hits. Downside: loses the retirement rationale documented in this plan; any future confusion must be resolved from memory or git history.

options.label: Other — specify retirement mechanism in freeform

items.text: Dependent-edge audit: only one other backlog item references `execute/vrooli-emulator-linux-first` — namely `execute/adopt-vrooli-emulator-in-deployment-flows`, which currently has depends_on = [mobile-operable-deployment-surfaces, qa-deployment-manager-code-quality-20260407, qa-scenario-to-desktop-code-quality-20260407, vrooli-emulator-linux-first, fix/qa-deployment-manager-tests-20260407]. After d2 resolves, the rewire replaces `vrooli-emulator-linux-first` with the chosen sibling set. No other items reference this umbrella, so rewire scope is tightly bounded to a single CLI call.

`acceptance_allow` mismatch: spec has `scenarios/vrooli-emulator/**, scenarios/scenario-to-desktop/**` — sensible for the former build scope but no longer aligned, since this item will make zero code changes in its retired form. Leaving the field unchanged is safe (no edits will be made that could violate it) and avoids spurious churn. If d3 chooses delete, the field vanishes with the item; if d3 chooses archive, the field becomes historical context. No auto-update recommended.
